subject: RFP: International data handling and export assurance workbook (NeuroHeal)
messages:
From: Sophie Marin <sophie.marin@neuroheal.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@neuroheal.com
Date: 2028-04-22T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: International data handling & cross-border safeguard details

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. As part of NeuroHeal's RFP we need a consolidated workbook that maps your controls to our cross-border transfer requirements and the DPA annex items (we added a checklist in the RFP). Specifically we need:

- A per-control mapping to GDPR Articles and the DPA Annex rows (data export legal basis, SCCs/DPF equivalence, subprocessor list, logging/audit controls).
- Evidence for cross-border safeguards (SCCs/DPF position statement, examples of contractual language you use).
- Operational details for EU-data: where is inference performed, whether tokenization/prefix caching exposes PHI, and how KMS/HSM is used.
- Retention and deletion flow for EU subject data and an example audit log extract.

Can you send a workbook and any sample evidence by EOD Wednesday (our procurement window is tight)? We'd also like a short 30-minute follow-up to review items we flag.

Thanks,
Sophie Marin
Senior Privacy Program Manager
NeuroHeal Therapeutics

Subject: Re: RFP: International data handling & cross-border safeguard details

Hi Sophie,

Appreciate the clarity — we've assembled a focused workbook that maps our controls to the RFP checklist and included explicit answers for the DPA annex items. Deliverables attached: export-assurance-workbook.xlsx and a compact network-architecture-diagram.png.

High-level summary:
- Legal basis / transfers: We support SCCs and our standard DPA Annex; where customers require a DPF equivalence statement we provide documented technical/contractual mitigations and can support Dedicated or Private deployment options as required.
- Runtime locality: By default hosted inference runs in the region requested (we route to EU regions for EU customers). For highest assurance we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated capacity to keep inference entirely within customer VPCs.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS supported via key-wrapping integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). HSM-backed key material is supported for Private deployments.
- Caching and KV stores: Prefix caching/kv is per-customer isolated; we can disable application-level prefix caching on request for sensitive workloads.

Can we book Wednesday 2028-04-24 10:00-10:30 AM CEST for a walkthrough? If that doesn't fit, propose 14:00 CEST.

Attachments: export-assurance-workbook.xlsx (workbook mapping), network-architecture-diagram.png (runtime sketch)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Sophie — following up with technical detail and the sample evidence you asked for. Key points below and I've uploaded a short technical appendix to the shared Drive link Kimberly sent.

1) EU data locality and inference execution - Our serving runtime selects region-local inference endpoints by default (EU-west, EU-central). For hosted customers we provision isolated model instances and per-customer routing. Dedicated/Private deployments provide strict network controls and do not traverse public backbone for request processing.

2) SCCs vs DPF and fallback options - We accept SCCs in our DPA. For customers requesting a DPF equivalence assessment we provide a documented set of technical mitigations (data minimization, encryption-in-flight and at-rest, KMS key separation, operational access controls, audit logs) and a DPF position statement signed by Head of Legal. Where contractual DPF equivalence is required, we recommend Either: (a) Dedicated capacity with contractual DPA Annex + SCCs; or (b) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for non-export-based assurance.

3) KMS/HSM and key custody - Supported modes: provider-managed keys (default), customer-provided keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed key wraps for Private installs. Crypto notes and example flow included in the Drive appendix.

4) Data flows, caching and PII exposure - Model input is transient. We automatically truncate/store only what customers elect to persist (e.g., for billing/analytics). Prefix/KV caches are tagged per-customer; for high-sensitivity flows we can disable caching and route to Dedicated.

5) Audit evidence and logs - Attached is a synthetic audit_log_sample.csv (sanitized) showing event types, timestamps, and request IDs. We also attach our SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted). Full SOC report available under NDA.

Attachments referenced: soc2-type2-summary.pdf (summary), audit_log_sample.csv (sanitized example)

If helpful, I can include a short runnable playbook showing how we configure a Dedicated tenant to avoid cross-border egress.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP: International data handling & cross-border safeguard details

Sophie — quick note from Security/Compliance to clarify the specific evidence items in the workbook (I've annotated Tab 2 of the workbook):

- Subprocessors: we provide a current subprocessor registry and commit to 30-day notification of changes. Link in the workbook points to the latest registry export.
- Logging / audit: logs include request id, model, region, start/end timestamps, and internal operator actions. The sanitized audit_log_sample.csv shows the fields we export on request.
- Retention & erasure: Subject data retention defaults are 30 days for short-term telemetry and 365 days max for customer-requested retention; we support custom retention settings and scripted erasure. Erasure requests produce an erasure confirmation token via the console or API.
- Controls & mappings: Control IDs in the workbook map to SOC 2/TISAX-like controls; where you need direct mapping to specific GDPR Articles we've added a crosswalk in Tab 3.
- DPA Annex redlines: Laura has prepared suggested contractual language for SCCs/DPA Annex clauses and a DocuSign envelope is ready if you want to start execution.

I also want to confirm that for EU-hosted inference we enforce TLS1.3, AES-256 at-rest, and we have role-based access controls with justification-required access for debug actions. For customers who need HSM key material, we can enable a BYOK + HSM mode in Private deployments.

DocuSign (DPA annex): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789
Drive workbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/NeuroHeal-Export-Workbook

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
